title: Carboxylic acids and derivatives
objectives: Recall ways of making carboxylic acids: oxidation of primary alcohols and aldehydes, hydrolysis of nitriles (acid or alkali) and hydrolysis of esters
Describe the reactions of carboxylic acids with reactive metals, alkalis, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates, alcohols (esterification) and LiAlH₄
Use mole ratios to calculate the amount of gas formed when acids react with metals and carbonates
Describe the formation of esters by condensation and name esters
Describe the hydrolysis of esters by dilute acid and by dilute alkali, and explain why the alkaline reaction goes to completion
prior: Nitriles from halogenoalkanes and HCN (Chapters 15 and 17)
why: Carboxylic acids and esters link everything you have met so far: alcohols, aldehydes and nitriles all lead to acids, and acids lead to esters. Paper 1 regularly asks you to count moles of gas from acids with several O–H groups and to name the products of ester hydrolysis.
intro: A carboxylic acid contains the carboxyl group, –COOH: a C=O and an O–H on the same carbon. That carbon is sp² (trigonal planar, about 120°). Carboxylic acids are weak acids: RCOOH ⇌ RCOO⁻ + H⁺, but much stronger than alcohols because the negative charge of RCOO⁻ is delocalised over two oxygen atoms.

head: starting material
reagent and conditions
example
rows: excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, heat under reflux
NaOH(aq), heat under reflux (gives the salt; acidify after)
dilute acid or NaOH(aq), heat under reflux

blocks.h: A nitrile route adds one carbon atom: halogenoalkane → (KCN in ethanol) → nitrile → (hydrolysis) → acid. So bromoethane gives propanoic acid. Oxidising an alcohol keeps the same number of carbons: 1-bromopropane → propan-1-ol → propanoic acid.

blocks.wrong: Heating a nitrile with NaOH(aq) gives the carboxylic acid.
blocks.right: In alkali you get the carboxylate salt (and NH₃ gas). Add dilute acid afterwards to obtain the free acid.

blocks.h: Counting gas: which O–H groups react?

Sodium is the only common reagent that reacts with alcohol OH groups as well as COOH groups. Carbonates, hydrogencarbonates and alkalis react only with the more acidic COOH groups. Use this to tell an alcohol group from an acid group.

blocks.name: acidgas
blocks.title: Gas from acids
blocks.h: Choose a compound and a reagent to see how many moles react and what volume of gas forms.

blocks.q: How many moles of H₂ form when 1 mol of citric-like acid HOOCCH₂C(OH)(COOH)CH₂COOH reacts with excess sodium? How many moles of CO₂ with excess NaHCO₃?
steps: count groups: 3 COOH and 1 alcohol OH
Na reacts with all 4 O–H: 4 × ½ = 2 mol H₂
NaHCO₃ reacts with the 3 COOH only: 3 mol CO₂
blocks.err: Letting NaHCO₃ react with the alcohol OH, or giving 1 mol H₂ per O–H with sodium.

blocks.h: Acid + alcohol, heated with a few drops of concentrated H₂SO₄ (catalyst), gives an ester and water: a condensation reaction. The reaction is reversible.

items: Name: alkyl group from the alcohol first, then the acid with -oic acid changed to -oate.
CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ is methyl propanoate (from propanoic acid and methanol).
In the formula RCOOR′, the part joined to C=O (RCO–) comes from the acid; –OR′ comes from the alcohol.

head: dilute acid (H₂SO₄ or HCl), reflux
dilute alkali (NaOH), reflux
rows: RCOO⁻ cannot react with the alcohol, so the back reaction cannot happen

blocks.name: esterbuild
blocks.title: Ester builder
blocks.h: Pick an acid and an alcohol to name the ester, then hydrolyse it with acid or alkali.

blocks.wrong: Propyl ethanoate gives propanoic acid when hydrolysed.
blocks.right: The -oate part names the acid: propyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol.

summary: Acids from: primary alcohols or aldehydes (K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺, reflux), nitriles (dilute acid, reflux; alkali gives the salt) and esters.
Halogenoalkane → nitrile → acid adds one carbon; halogenoalkane → alcohol → acid keeps the chain length.
Acid + metal → salt + H₂ (redox); + alkali → salt + water; + carbonate/hydrogencarbonate → salt + water + CO₂.
Na reacts with every O–H (½ H₂ each); carbonates and NaHCO₃ react only with COOH.
LiAlH₄ (not NaBH₄) reduces RCOOH to RCH₂OH.
Esterification: acid + alcohol, conc. H₂SO₄, heat; condensation; reversible. Name alkyl … -oate.
Acid hydrolysis of an ester: equilibrium, acid + alcohol. Alkaline hydrolysis: complete, carboxylate salt + alcohol.

flash.q: Reagent and conditions: primary alcohol → carboxylic acid?
flash.a: Excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, heat under reflux

flash.q: Reagent and conditions: nitrile → carboxylic acid?
Organic product when a nitrile is heated with NaOH(aq)?
Which O–H groups does Na react with?
Which O–H groups does Na₂CO₃ react with?
Moles of CO₂ per COOH with NaHCO₃?
Type of reaction: acid + alcohol → ester?
Products of acid hydrolysis of an ester?
Products of alkaline hydrolysis of an ester?
Why does alkaline hydrolysis go to completion?
flash.a: RCOO⁻ cannot react with the alcohol

practice.q: Give a two-step route from 1-bromopropane to butanoic acid, with reagents and conditions.
practice.a: KCN in ethanol, heat under reflux → butanenitrile; then dilute HCl, heat under reflux → butanoic acid.

practice.q: Write equations for propanoic acid with (a) magnesium and (b) sodium carbonate.
Calculate the volume of H₂ at room conditions when 0.0200 mol of HOCH₂COOH reacts with excess sodium.
practice.a: Two O–H groups → 0.0200 mol H₂ → 0.0200 × 24.0 = 0.480 dm³ (480 cm³).

practice.q: Name the ester formed from butanoic acid and ethanol and write the equation.
practice.a: Ethyl butanoate; CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃CH₂CH₂COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.

practice.q: Give the products when methyl ethanoate is refluxed with (a) dilute H₂SO₄ and (b) NaOH(aq).
practice.a: (a) ethanoic acid and methanol (equilibrium); (b) sodium ethanoate and methanol.

practice.q: Explain why alkaline hydrolysis of an ester gives a better yield than acid hydrolysis.
practice.a: In alkali the acid is converted to the carboxylate ion, which cannot react with the alcohol, so the reaction is not reversible and goes to completion; acid hydrolysis reaches an equilibrium.

assessment.q: Which reagent gives CO₂ with ethanoic acid?
Hydrolysing propanenitrile with dilute HCl gives…
Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate gives…
Moles of H₂ from 1 mol HOCH₂COOH with excess Na?

assessment.why: Water is eliminated as two molecules join.

assessment.q: Acid hydrolysis of an ester is…
Which of these is a redox reaction?
assessment.why: Mg oxidised; H⁺ reduced to H₂.

assessment_s.q:
Lactic acid is CH₃CH(OH)COOH.
(a) Calculate the volume of gas at room conditions when 0.0100 mol of lactic acid reacts with (i) excess Na, (ii) excess NaHCO₃. [2]
(b) Lactic acid can be made from ethanal in two steps. Give the reagents and conditions. [2]
(c) Lactic acid is heated with methanol and a little conc. H₂SO₄. Give the structural formula and name of the ester. [2]
assessment_s.a:
(a)(i) 2 O–H → 0.0100 mol H₂ = 240 cm³; (ii) 1 COOH → 0.0100 mol CO₂ = 240 cm³
(b) HCN with a little KCN; then heat under reflux with dilute HCl
(c) CH₃CH(OH)COOCH₃, methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate

assessment_s.q:
Ethyl propanoate is hydrolysed.
(a) Write equations for its hydrolysis by (i) dilute H₂SO₄ and (ii) NaOH(aq). [2]
(b) Explain why (ii) goes to completion but (i) does not. [2]
(c) Starting from 1 mol of ester, calculate the total mass of organic products in (ii). [Mr: CH₃CH₂COONa 96.0; C₂H₅OH 46.0] [1]
assessment_s.a:
(a)(i) CH₃CH₂COOC₂H₅ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃CH₂COOH + C₂H₅OH; (ii) CH₃CH₂COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃CH₂COONa + C₂H₅OH
(b) acid hydrolysis is the reverse of esterification and reaches equilibrium; in alkali the carboxylate ion formed cannot react with ethanol, so there is no back reaction
(c) 96.0 + 46.0 = 142.0 g

pp.skill: A one-step route to a carboxylic acid
pp.mis: Forgetting that a nitrile adds a carbon or that an ester gives the other acid
pp.stem: Which starting material could be converted into butanoic acid in a single reaction?
pp.exp: Butanal is oxidised by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ (reflux) to butanoic acid. Propanenitrile hydrolyses to propanoic acid; butan-2-ol gives butanone; butyl ethanoate hydrolyses to ethanoic acid and butan-1-ol.

pp.skill: Reactions that produce a carboxylic acid
pp.mis: Thinking NaBH₄ or Na oxidises
pp.stem:
Three mixtures are heated under reflux. Which produce propanoic acid as one product?
1 propanal + acidified K₂Cr₂O₇
2 propan-1-ol + NaBH₄
3 propanenitrile + dilute HCl
pp.exp: Oxidising the aldehyde and acid-hydrolysing the nitrile both give CH₃CH₂COOH. NaBH₄ is a reducing agent and does not react with an alcohol.

pp.skill: Identifying a nitrile from its hydrolysis product
pp.mis: Choosing a nitrile with one carbon too few
pp.stem: W contains only carbon, hydrogen and nitrogen. W is heated with HCl(aq) to give butanoic acid. Which is correct?
pp.exp: RC≡N + 2H₂O + HCl → RCOOH + NH₄Cl. The nitrile carbon becomes the COOH carbon, so the chain length is unchanged: butanenitrile, CH₃CH₂CH₂CN → CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH.

pp.skill: Reagents for halogenoalkane → nitrile → acid
pp.mis: Using HCN or NH₃ in the first step
pp.stem: Bromoethane is converted into propanoic acid in two steps via CH₃CH₂CN. Which reagents are used?
opts: step 1 KCN in ethanol; step 2 HCl(aq), heat
step 1 KCN in water; step 2 Na₂CO₃(aq)
pp.exp: KCN in ethanol substitutes CN for Br (chain + 1 C). Heating the nitrile under reflux with dilute acid hydrolyses it to CH₃CH₂COOH. NaOH(aq) would give the salt, not the acid.

pp.skill: Choosing a route that keeps the chain length
pp.mis: Using KCN, which lengthens the chain
pp.stem: 1-chlorobutane is converted into butanoic acid by treatment with reagent X and then reagent Y. What are X and Y?
opts: X NaOH(aq), heat; Y acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, reflux
X KCN in ethanol; Y HCl(aq)
X KCN in ethanol; Y NaOH(aq)
pp.exp: Substitution gives butan-1-ol; oxidation under reflux gives butanoic acid (4 C). The KCN routes give a 5-carbon product (pentanoic acid or its salt).

pp.skill: Mass of salt from alkaline hydrolysis of a nitrile
pp.mis: Using the Mr of the free acid
pp.stem: 0.250 mol of propanenitrile is heated with excess NaOH(aq). The only products are organic compound S and ammonia. The yield is 75.0%. [Mr: CH₃CH₂COOH, 74.0; CH₃CH₂COONa, 96.0; CH₃COONa, 82.0] What mass of S is formed?
pp.exp: In alkali the product is the salt: CH₃CH₂CN + NaOH + H₂O → CH₃CH₂COONa + NH₃. 0.250 × 96.0 × 0.750 = 18.0 g.

pp.skill: Shape change when a nitrile is hydrolysed
pp.mis: Thinking the COOH carbon is tetrahedral
pp.stem: Propanenitrile is heated under reflux with dilute HCl to give propanoic acid. What are the C–C≡N angle in propanenitrile and the O=C–O angle in propanoic acid?
pp.exp: The nitrile carbon has two electron regions (one σ to C, one triple bond): linear, 180°. The COOH carbon has three regions (sp²): trigonal planar, about 120°.

pp.skill: Following nitrile → acid → alcohol
pp.mis: Classifying the alcohol by the branching rather than the C–OH carbon
pp.stem: (CH₃)₂CHCN is heated with H⁺(aq) to give X. X is then reduced with LiAlH₄ to alcohol Y. Which row is correct?
pp.exp: Hydrolysis: (CH₃)₂CHCOOH, 2-methylpropanoic acid. LiAlH₄ reduces COOH to CH₂OH: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH. The C–OH carbon is bonded to one other carbon, so Y is primary.

pp.skill: Correct equations for reactions of acids
pp.mis: Forgetting H₂ from a metal or writing H₂ from esterification
pp.stem:
Which equations are correct?
1 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂
2 CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
3 CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂
pp.exp: Metals give a salt and H₂; hydrogencarbonates give a salt, water and CO₂. Esterification eliminates water, not hydrogen.

pp.skill: Which reagents form carboxylate ions
pp.mis: Thinking an ester or reduction product contains carboxylate ions
pp.stem:
Propanoic acid is mixed in turn with:
1 magnesium ribbon
2 sodium tetrahydridoborate
3 warm ethanol plus a drop of conc. H₂SO₄
Which mixture(s) end up containing CH₃CH₂COO⁻ ions?
pp.exp: Mg forms magnesium propanoate, (CH₃CH₂COO⁻)₂Mg²⁺. NaBH₄ does not reduce acids; ethanol forms a covalent ester, ethyl propanoate, with no ions.

pp.skill: Recognising redox in acid reactions
pp.mis: Calling every reaction of an acid redox
pp.stem: Consider: (1) Mg ribbon dropped into CH₃COOH(aq); (2) CH₃COOH(aq) titrated with NaOH(aq). In which do oxidation numbers change?
pp.exp: In 1, Mg goes from 0 to +2 and H from +1 to 0 (H₂ forms): redox. In 2, H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O: neutralisation, no oxidation number changes.

pp.skill: Deducing a structure from Na, Na₂CO₃ and dichromate tests
pp.mis: Forgetting that primary and secondary OH groups are oxidised
pp.stem: X contains C, H and O only. X fizzes with Na and with Na₂CO₃, and stays orange when heated with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇. What could X be?
pp.exp: Fizzing with Na₂CO₃ → COOH. No oxidation → no CHO and no primary or secondary OH. 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanoic acid has a tertiary OH, which is not oxidised.

pp.skill: Comparing gas volumes with Na and Na₂CO₃
pp.mis: Forgetting that Na also reacts with alcohol OH groups
pp.stem: 1 mol of each compound reacts separately with excess Na and with excess Na₂CO₃. Which gives the same volume of gas with both reagents?
pp.exp: Each COOH gives ½ H₂ with Na and ½ CO₂ with Na₂CO₃. Each alcohol OH gives ½ H₂ with Na but nothing with Na₂CO₃. Only propanedioic acid has no alcohol OH: 1 mol H₂ and 1 mol CO₂.

pp.skill: Gas volumes from an acid with a metal and a carbonate
pp.mis: Doubling the H₂ from Mg because Mg is 2+
pp.stem: 3.00 g of ethanoic acid (Mr 60.0) reacts completely with excess Mg. A second 3.00 g sample reacts completely with excess Na₂CO₃. What volumes of gas form at room conditions?
pp.exp: n(acid) = 0.0500 mol. 2CH₃COOH + Mg → … + H₂: 0.0250 mol H₂. 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → … + CO₂ + H₂O: 0.0250 mol CO₂. Each is 0.0250 × 24 000 = 600 cm³.

pp.skill: Mole ratios for a hydroxy dicarboxylic acid
pp.mis: Counting only the COOH groups for sodium
pp.stem: Malic acid is HOOCCH(OH)CH₂COOH. Which substance reacts with 1 mol of malic acid in a 3 : 1 mole ratio (3 mol of the substance per mol of acid)?
pp.exp: Na reacts with all three O–H groups (two COOH and one alcohol OH): 3 mol. NaOH and NaHCO₃ react only with the two COOH groups (2 mol); Na₂CO₃ needs 1 mol.

pp.skill: Ranking gas volumes from several reactions
pp.mis: Forgetting NaOH gives no gas
pp.stem:
1 mol of each compound reacts with an excess of the reagent shown:
W HOOCCH₂COOH + Na
X HOCH₂COOH + Na₂CO₃
Y HOCH₂COOH + NaOH
Z HOOCCH(OH)CH₂COOH + Na
What is the order from greatest to least volume of gas?
pp.exp: Z: three O–H → 1.5 mol H₂. W: two COOH → 1 mol H₂. X: one COOH → 0.5 mol CO₂. Y: neutralisation → no gas.

pp.skill: Mr of products of reactions of an acid
pp.mis: Ignoring that the calcium salt contains two anions
pp.stem: Propanoic acid reacts separately with each substance. Which gives the organic product with the highest Mr?
pp.exp: Calcium propanoate (CH₃CH₂COO)₂Ca, Mr 186. Sodium propanoate 96; butyl propanoate 130; propan-1-ol 60.

pp.skill: Product of a dicarboxylic acid with excess alkali
pp.mis: Neutralising only one COOH
pp.stem: Excess NaOH(aq) is added to propanedioic acid, HOOCCH₂COOH. What is the organic product?
pp.exp: With excess alkali both COOH groups lose H⁺, giving the dicarboxylate ion (as its disodium salt).

pp.skill: Deducing a structure from Na, Na₂CO₃ and Fehling’s
pp.mis: Choosing a compound that is already an acid
pp.stem: Y, C₄H₆O₂, reacts with Na but not with Na₂CO₃. After warming with Fehling’s reagent and acidifying, the organic product reacts with both Na and Na₂CO₃. What could Y be?
pp.exp: Y has an alcohol OH (Na yes, Na₂CO₃ no) and a CHO group, which Fehling’s oxidises to COOH. The acid would already react with Na₂CO₃; the dialdehyde and the diketone have no OH.

pp.skill: Products of reducing acids with excess LiAlH₄
pp.mis: Stopping at the aldehyde with excess LiAlH₄
pp.stem:
P, C₄H₈O₂, is a carboxylic acid that reacts with excess LiAlH₄ to give Q. Which pairs could be P and Q?
1 CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH
2 (CH₃)₂CHCOOH → (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH
3 CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH → CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO
pp.exp: With excess LiAlH₄, RCOOH + 4[H] → RCH₂OH + H₂O. The reduction does not stop at the aldehyde, and the carbon skeleton is unchanged.

pp.skill: Acid → alcohol → alkene
pp.mis: Choosing NaBH₄ or ethanolic NaOH
pp.stem: Butanoic acid is converted into but-1-ene in two steps. Which reagents are used?
opts: step 1 LiAlH₄; step 2 conc. H₂SO₄, heat
step 1 LiAlH₄; step 2 NaOH in ethanol
step 1 NaBH₄; step 2 NaOH in ethanol
pp.exp: Only LiAlH₄ reduces a carboxylic acid (to butan-1-ol). Dehydration of the alcohol needs a concentrated acid (or hot Al₂O₃); ethanolic NaOH eliminates from halogenoalkanes, not alcohols.

pp.skill: Reduction followed by esterification
pp.mis: Naming the ester the wrong way round
pp.stem: Ethanoic acid is reduced by LiAlH₄ to P. P then reacts with propanoic acid and a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ to give Q. What are P and Q?
pp.exp: LiAlH₄ reduces CH₃COOH to CH₃CH₂OH. With propanoic acid this gives CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃: the acid part (propanoate) comes from propanoic acid and the alkyl part (ethyl) from ethanol.

pp.skill: Type of reaction and catalyst for esterification
pp.mis: Calling it hydrolysis or using NaOH
pp.stem: Ethyl propanoate is made from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol with a catalyst. Which row describes the reaction?
pp.exp: Two molecules join with loss of water: a condensation reaction. Concentrated H₂SO₄ is the catalyst (it also helps by removing water). NaOH would hydrolyse esters.

pp.skill: Which acid and alcohol make a given ester
pp.mis: Swapping the acid and alcohol parts
pp.stem: Which pair could react to give CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₃?
pp.exp: The C=O end (CH₃CH₂CH₂CO–) comes from butanoic acid; –OCH₃ comes from methanol. The ester is methyl butanoate.

pp.skill: Products of alkaline ester hydrolysis
pp.mis: Giving the free acid in alkaline conditions
pp.stem: HCOOCH₂CH₃ is refluxed with NaOH(aq). Which two organic substances are present at the end?
pp.exp: In alkali the acid part is released as its salt: HCOOCH₂CH₃ + NaOH → HCOONa + CH₃CH₂OH.

pp.skill: Identifying one product of alkaline hydrolysis
pp.mis: Giving an alkoxide ion
pp.stem: Which compound is a product of heating CH₃CH₂COOCH(CH₃)₂ with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
pp.exp: The products are sodium propanoate and propan-2-ol. The alcohol is formed as the neutral alcohol, not an alkoxide; the acid is formed as its salt, not the free acid.

pp.skill: Products of acid ester hydrolysis
pp.mis: Giving the carboxylate ion in acid
pp.stem: An ester R′COOR″ is heated under reflux with dilute sulfuric acid. What are the products?
opts: R′COOH and R″OH, in an equilibrium mixture
pp.exp: Acid hydrolysis is the reverse of esterification and is reversible: R′COOR″ + H₂O ⇌ R′COOH + R″OH.

pp.skill: Comparing acid and alkaline hydrolysis
pp.mis: Thinking acid hydrolysis goes to completion
pp.stem: Which comparison of hydrolysing an ester with aqueous alkali and with aqueous acid is correct?
opts: alkali: equilibrium, salt + alcohol; acid: complete, acid + alcohol
alkali: complete, salt + alcohol; acid: equilibrium, acid + alcohol
alkali: complete, acid + alcohol; acid: complete, salt + alcohol
alkali: equilibrium, acid + alcohol; acid: equilibrium, salt + alcohol
pp.exp: The carboxylate ion formed in alkali cannot react with the alcohol, so the reaction goes to completion. In acid the reaction is reversible.

pp.skill: Percentage by mass of hydrolysis products
pp.mis: Using the free acid instead of its salt
pp.stem: Methyl butanoate is heated under reflux with aqueous NaOH. The two organic products are separated and weighed. What percentage of the total mass is each product? [Mr: CH₃CH₂CH₂COONa 110.0; CH₃OH 32.0]

pp.skill: Acids from hydrolysing a mixture of esters
pp.mis: Taking the acid from the alkyl part
pp.stem: A mixture of methyl propanoate, ethyl methanoate, propyl ethanoate and methyl ethanoate is heated with NaOH(aq), then acidified. Which carboxylic acids are present?
pp.exp: The second word of each name gives the acid: propanoate → propanoic, methanoate → methanoic, ethanoate → ethanoic (twice).

pp.skill: Which reaction gives a particular free acid
pp.mis: Forgetting alkali gives the salt
pp.stem: Which reaction has propanoic acid as one of its products?
opts: CH₃CN heated under reflux with dilute acid
CH₃CH₂CN heated under reflux with dilute alkali
CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ heated under reflux with dilute acid
HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃ heated under reflux with dilute acid
pp.exp: Acid hydrolysis of methyl propanoate gives propanoic acid and methanol. CH₃CN gives ethanoic acid; alkali gives sodium propanoate; propyl methanoate gives methanoic acid.

pp.skill: Which compounds give a given acid on acid hydrolysis
pp.mis: Looking at the wrong side of the ester
pp.stem:
Which compounds produce ethanoic acid when heated with HCl(aq)?
1 CH₃COOCH₂CH₃
2 CH₃CH₂CN
3 HCOOCH₂CH₃
pp.exp: Ethyl ethanoate → ethanoic acid + ethanol. Propanenitrile → propanoic acid. Ethyl methanoate → methanoic acid + ethanol.

pp.skill: Esters and nitriles that hydrolyse to a given acid
pp.mis: Thinking a propyl ester gives propanoic acid
pp.stem:
Which two compounds, heated separately with dilute H₂SO₄, give propanoic acid?
1 methyl propanoate
2 propyl ethanoate
3 propanenitrile
4 ethanenitrile
pp.exp: Methyl propanoate → propanoic acid + methanol; propanenitrile → propanoic acid. Propyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol; ethanenitrile gives ethanoic acid.

pp.skill: Counting esters of one acid, including stereoisomers
pp.mis: Missing the chiral butyl group
pp.stem: Include optical isomers. Ethanoic acid is esterified with each alcohol of formula C₄H₁₀O in turn. How many different C₆H₁₂O₂ esters (counting enantiomers separately) result?
pp.exp: CH₃COO–C₄H₉ with the four butyl groups: butyl, 2-methylpropyl, 1,1-dimethylethyl and 1-methylpropyl. The 1-methylpropyl (butan-2-yl) ester has a chiral carbon, giving two enantiomers: 5.

pp.skill: Counting all products from hydrolysing a set of isomeric esters
pp.mis: Counting ethanoic acid or an alcohol twice
pp.stem: Every ester with formula C₄H₈O₂ is refluxed separately with dilute acid. Altogether, how many different organic products appear?
pp.exp: The esters are HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃, HCOOCH(CH₃)₂, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH₂COOCH₃. Products: methanoic acid, propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol, ethanoic acid, ethanol, propanoic acid, methanol = 7.

pp.skill: Reducing an acid and lengthening the chain via a nitrile
pp.stem: Butanoic acid can be reduced, and the alcohol formed can be converted into a longer-chain acid.

parts.q: Give the formula of the reducing agent and complete the equation: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH + …[H] →
Butan-1-ol reacts with SOCl₂ to give compound E. Name the type of reaction and give the formula of E.
Give the reagent and conditions to turn E into pentanenitrile.
ms: KCN in ethanol, heat under reflux

parts.q: Pentanenitrile is heated with NaOH(aq). Write an equation and name the type of reaction.

pp.skill: Nitrile hydrolysis then esterification
pp.stem: 2-bromobutane, CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₃, is converted to nitrile U, then to carboxylic acid V, which is then esterified.

parts.q: Give the reagent and conditions for 2-bromobutane → U.
ms: KCN in ethanol, heat under reflux

parts.q: U is hydrolysed by heating with HCl(aq). Write an equation and name V.
V reacts with methanol and a little conc. H₂SO₄. Name the type of reaction, the functional group formed and give the molecular formula of the product.
